title: a large indexed directory vanishing costs a refresh one delete per path
body:
Measured 2026-09-14 by dc in a private worktree: the index held a directory of build output (a worktree's in-tree cargo target, ~190k paths, 190507 of them `index_file` skip rows) under the index scope. The directory was removed, and the next whole-scope refresh (`index_refresh(None)`, reached through `intent mcp`'s search) ran at ~90-98% of one core for 8+ minutes and did not finish before it was stopped: `changed_under` reports every vanished path, and `apply_index_changes`, `replace_sections_for` and `replace_symbols_for` each delete per path (with FTS5 secure-delete since rung 26). A wholesale `intent index rebuild` of the same tree took about a minute.

Not fixed here. Two questions: whether a refresh should switch to a wholesale replace past some count of removals; and whether an in-tree cargo target dir that is not gitignored (a private worktree's `target-dc/`) should ever be inside the index scope at all.



CLOSED 2026-09-14 (dc): a scoped index delete is one statement per table. `apply_index_changes`, `replace_sections_for` and `replace_symbols_for` stage the paths into a per-connection temporary table, `temp.gone`, and delete `WHERE path IN (SELECT path FROM temp.gone)`. Before, they ran one `DELETE` per path, and each of those scanned a whole FTS5 table, which cannot look a row up by path.

Judged by one timed drive (scratchpad batch/drive-0393.txt): a 10,000-file indexed directory vanishes, then one `intent search` reconciles. The base binary took 36 s and the fix 1 s, and both left 0 rows under the directory. The index tests pass, and so does the batch's full run.

Not built here, and left to a ruling if wanted: the issue's second question, whether an in-tree target dir that is not gitignored belongs inside the index scope.
